intro.title: Running waves
intro.subtitle: Lesson 7: /wavecoord:wave-run
intro.say: In this lesson we run a wave: what wave run picks, what the workers do, and the settings that keep a wave safe.

intro.title: The knobs
bullets: wip_cap: the most attempts in flight. Start with 2 or 3.
exec: model, effort, max_turns, budget_usd, timeout_min per task.
claude_flags: what an unattended worker may run.
check_cmd: your tests, run before each merge.
intro.say: A few settings control a wave. W I P cap limits the workers in flight. Each task's exec block sets its model, turns, budget and timeout. The host's claude flags decide what a worker may run. And the check command runs your tests before each merge.

outro.title: The fence, in stages
outro.say: The edit fence checks that a worker writes only the paths of its lease, at five points from the edit to the merge. Start in advisory mode. After a few clean waves, set push and merge to enforce, then edit. Protected paths always wait for your yes.

steps.say: The to-do app again, with the due-dates plan merged: three tasks in two waves.
This demo has no GitHub account. Its origin is a folder on this machine, and gh talks to a local stand-in for GitHub, so the commands look the same as on GitHub.
This is the config. One local host with two slots, a W I P cap of two, the fence in advisory mode, and the test suite as the check command. Workers may edit files, commit, and run Python.
A task. It owns two paths, the module and its test. Its exec block runs it on haiku, with at most thirty turns, one dollar and twenty minutes.
Wave run checks the coordinator, reads the ready tasks, and picks the ones whose paths do not overlap.
Two tasks started. The third needs both, so it waits for the next wave.
Each worker runs in its own git worktree, on its own branch. It cannot push: when it ends, the launcher pushes the branch and the worker posts one report.
The fence is in advisory mode: a write outside the lease is a warning, not a stop.
Now we wait for the workers. We skip ahead.
Both workers reported, with their turns and cost. Their branches are pushed. Opening the pull requests and merging is triage, in lesson nine.
